original_method: Master remains TBD. Review identifies Sensor/Event 0x04/0x2a only as a guarded target-approved mutation after the exact sensor and all-events or event-mask scope are established.
manual_activity: Owner verifies the sensor and its threshold/discrete event model, approves the exact re-arm-all or individual assertion/deassertion scope, and decides how to handle an active fault that immediately reasserts.
required_inputs: Validated sensor number and SDR identity
Sensor type and supported event capability

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: DeepSeek correctly refuses to invent a re-arm vector from TBD source text; execution becomes possible only with a sensor-type-aware package and explicit scope approval.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After fresh approval, use protected `ipmitool raw 0x04 0x2a <validated-sensor> <approved-rearm-selector-and-mask-bytes>` with the complete target-defined schema, then query 0x04/0x2b after the defined sensor update window.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Master TBD and 10/5 timing remain unchanged; no sensor number, mask, all-event scope or update delay is fabricated.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the re-arm to a verified sensor/event representation, preserve pre-state, approve the exact narrow scope, execute once, then verify the selected latched status and record any reassertion while proving monitoring configuration and logs were preserved.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds the missing target, mask, approval, status-oracle and no-retry controls without changing Master.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Read-only status collection is necessary evidence but cannot satisfy the functional re-arm objective; command completion alone also does not prove the requested event bits cleared or remained cleared.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Re-arming can remove valuable latched diagnostic state, and a wrong sensor or broad mask can obscure fault history. An active condition may reassert immediately and must not trigger an automatic loop.

project_override_considerations: A vendor API may replace raw IPMI only when it targets the same sensor/event bits, preserves pre/post evidence, has identical blast radius and documents whether 0x04/0x2a itself remains unverified.
expected_evidence: Sensor type, event capability and approved scope
Fresh confirmation containing the exact request bytes
Preserved pre-state event status and event-enable context
Post-update event status with requested bit comparison
Immediate reassertion and active-fault context if present
Unchanged thresholds, hysteresis, enables and unrelated-sensor audit

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Items require a monitoring-state mutation, but Procedure and Criteria are TBD and the generic pre-step would clear diagnostic logs. DeepSeek therefore has no executable method. Review preserves the conflict and supplies a conditional, sensor-scoped transaction rather than treating a read-only query as full coverage.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The re-arm function and command family are identifiable. Sensor identity, exact event scope, acceptance timing and fresh approval are project execution-readiness inputs, so review can complete without executing or guessing them.

review_improvement: Defines the difference between re-arm-all and selective event masks, ties the operation to SDR capability and a status oracle, preserves evidence, limits execution to one confirmed mutation and handles reassertion without retries.
independent_technical_reasoning: Re-arm changes latched event state rather than sensor thresholds or event-enable configuration. Its safe unit of work is therefore one verified sensor plus an explicit event-bit scope. Verification must compare pre/post status after the platform update window and distinguish a successful re-arm followed by legitimate active-fault reassertion from command failure. Clearing logs or repeating the request would destroy exactly the evidence needed for that distinction.
